title: Why Is Venus 464°C While Uranus Drops to −224°C?
description:
Every Planet Explained in 12 Minutes (Mercury to Neptune)

Why is Venus's surface 464 degrees Celsius while Uranus's air drops to minus 224? As an ice giant, Uranus has no true surface — minus 224.2 °C (49 K) is its coldest atmospheric minimum, colder than Neptune in some places. On Venus, a thick 96.5% carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat in a runaway greenhouse and bakes its surface to 464 °C (737 K).

Sources: Williams, D. R. (2024), NASA Goddard NSSDCA Venus Fact Sheet (737 K / 464 °C mean surface temperature, 96.5% CO2 atmosphere) · NASA Science Venus Facts (thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect) · NASA Science Uranus Facts (no true surface; 49 K / −224.2 °C minimum atmospheric temperature, colder than Neptune in some places).

Pictures: Real NASA and ESA space imagery and official NASA Goddard Scientific Visualization Studio planetary visualizations, cropped, colour-graded and animated with smooth camera moves, paired with AI-assisted British narration (ElevenLabs Ben Orbit Narrator). Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio / Johns Hopkins APL / Naval Research Laboratory (Parker Solar Probe Venus flyby visualization & WISPR/Magellan 3rd flyby, SVS 14095); NASA Solar Dynamics Observatory (AIA 171 Å Venus transit); NASA Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS 20390 Shot 8 Uranus); ESA/Webb, NASA, CSA, STScI (JWST NIRCam Uranus rings and polar cap, weic2332a, CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); NASA/JPL-Caltech (Voyager 2 Uranus PIA01488; Magellan synthetic aperture radar Venus surface PIA00215).
